title: Brazilian Black Bean Stew
subtitle: Feijoada-style pork and black bean stew
excerpt: A rich, smoky stew of black beans, chorizo, and pork belly inspired by the Brazilian feijoada tradition. It takes about an hour on the hob and the flavour deepens considerably the next day. Serve with rice and a squeeze of orange as tradition dictates.
sourceNotes: Inspired by the Brazilian national dish feijoada. Traditionally made with cured and smoked pork cuts; this version uses chorizo and pork belly as accessible substitutes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight and reheat gently with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a very large stockpot.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Improves overnight. Make the day before and reheat gently.

content.text: Traditional feijoada is garnished with orange slices; the citrus cuts through the richness of the beans and pork. Use the zest in the stew itself and serve the rest of the orange alongside.
Heat the olive oil in a stockpot over a medium-high heat. Add the pork belly chunks and brown on all sides for about 5 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add the chorizo and cook for 3 minutes until it releases its oil and starts to colour at the edges.
Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika and cook for 2 minutes.
Return the pork belly to the pot. Add the black beans, bay leaves, orange zest, and 500ml of water.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 40 minutes until the pork is very tender and the stew has thickened.
Remove the bay leaves. Season with salt. Mash a few ladles of beans against the side of the pot to further thicken the stew if needed.
Serve with rice and orange slices on the side.

items.fix: Remove the lid and simmer for 10 minutes more.
Add a splash of water, re-cover, and cook for 20 minutes more.
